name: Monotron Whalesong
description:
A synthy whale-song-like sound suitable for horror and general creepiness.

Made using a Korg Monotron into a Zoom MS-70CDR - if you like making reverby ambient sounds, I can't recommend this pedal enough! It's affordable, tough, user-friendly and sounds AWESOME.

name: Nemean Roar.wav
description: A roar for a Kaiju style creature. Lions, tigers, bears and a hint of whale song. Most of the sounds (a couple of bass instruments, several animal roars) come from Garageband, along with some recordings of a human  made on a Zoom H1. All mixed together in Final Cut Pro X with some pitch and reverb effects thrown on top for good measure. For attribution, please credit www.laughingwiththestorm.net

name: Dolphin Song 2.mp3
description: This is a lightly processed version of my latest sound, Dolphin Song 1. I added a little echo, reverb, and eq to bring out that underwater/dolphin sound a little. Enjoy.

name: Ambience_Whalesong
description:
Wow, I've never heard whales singing before! These... are whales, right?


Inhuman whalings with long and spacious echo. These were made with modulated sinewaves spliced with irresponsible amounts of saturation, some wave freezing, then fed into a reverb-delay chain.

name: MBARI_MARS_2017_1107h22_HumpbackWhaleSongSession.wav
description:
Are you a fan of humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) song? If so, then the MBARI_MARS long playing (LP) series of humpback whale song recordings is for you. This recording is the first in the series.

Each of these recordings contains hours of continuous song captured with a quiet ocean background in deep water off Santa Cruz, California. These recordings are from an oceanic soundscape project. More information is available about this research and education project as well as the occurrence of humpback whale song off central California.

The recording was made on 7 November 2017 and is available for your creative endeavors under the Creative Commons license. Please acknowledge Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute as the source of the recording.

name: Whale Boy
description: A short, abstract soundscape with a whale song quality. Recorded live to disc in Logic and processed with time stretching in WaveLab.

name: Dolphin Song 1.mp3
description: I accientally discovered this sound when I was erasing a whiteboard with my finger. I immediately hooked up my SM-57 and ran my finger over the whiteboard at various speeds for a couple minutes to get the sound we have here. I didn't add any reverb or other effects to the sound so people could do there own thing with it, so it's a little dry right now. But it'll dress up nicely I think.

name: DeepCheering.wav
description: Whales cheering and clapping. Actually this started out as humans clapping and cheering, from the end of ChristmasMarchingBandSong.wav. The part in the middle sounds a bit like distant sirens.

name: Ruiz_Ylona_2019_2020_handspinner_painting_metalpliers.wav
description:
For this sound I used my first "whale song" noise as background noise. then I used a spray paint for the "pshiiiit" as well as the spray cap for the "clap"
we also hear the handspinner rubbing with metal pliers.
I modified the sounds one by one which I then assembled on protools to obtain a slightly more complex result.
I played on reverb, distortion, echo and diffusion to get something metallic and psychadelic.I admit that there is a bit of improvisation, hazard and chance
